phase_note: Amendment 1 (2026-07-26, revised at the design gate) reopened this implemented spec WITHOUT reopening any shipped behavior: all 20 execution units of the first pass remain in place and none is rewritten. Requirements were auto-approved at the design gate (-y) and design.md has now been regenerated in merge mode against them -- the first pass's content is preserved verbatim except for the four formula-pinning notes that named docs/reference/fitdocs-ai-reference.md as a source (AggregateMetrics, PowerSeriesMetrics, StressMetrics, and the Req 7/8/9/11 traceability rows), which Req 15.5 forbids. Added to design.md: a citation layer (src/fitdocs/citation.py) owning the shared VerificationStatus/Citation/FitdocsChoice/Departure/CitedConstant vocabulary at the bottom of the dependency graph, a MetricsSources records module, a two-part ConstantGuard (registry assertions plus a numeric-literal scan that can fail for an UNregistered constant, which is what carries Req 16.3), a MigrationGate tying a changed value to the DOC_VERSION advance, TrimpWeighting/TrimpResult for Req 17, and an Amendment 1 sourcing-gate section stating the Req 15.4 block explicitly. All 98 criteria appear in the design's traceability; nothing renumbered. tasks.md has NOT been regenerated against this amendment and its approval is therefore reset to false; design approval is the next gate. CONSTANT-COUNT RECONCILIATION, CORRECTED (2026-07-27, queue item 2026-07-26-amendment-1-constant-count-ambiguous, REOPENED not closed -- see below). Criterion 15.6 enumerates seven comma-delimited items, one of which names two constants (the training-impulse weighting's coefficient and exponent), so seven items cover eight named constants; requirements.md's Revision narrative, design.md's MetricsSources note, and this record's amendments[0].revision and amendments[0].design text all now state that reading explicitly, and no criterion is renumbered or withdrawn. Convention for this array going forward: amendments[*] entries are dated records of what was measured or ruled at the time and are left verbatim once written; a later correction is appended as a new dated note rather than rewritten into the original entry. amendments[0].reason's 'Measured surface before deciding' list is an exception to that convention -- it was edited in place (the NP averaging exponent added, since it was missing and is the value most exposed to an undercount) rather than left as originally measured with a separate correcting annotation. That in-place edit forecloses a second reading under which 'seven' meant seven MEASURED constants -- the original list already counted the TRIMP coefficient and exponent as two separate items and omitted only the averaging exponent, so under that second reading the omission might have been the deliberate boundary of what 'measured' meant, not an oversight. FLAGGED FOR THE MAINTAINER, not decided by this session: the reopened queue item below states the question and notes plainly that the edit as it stands forecloses reading (B). The prior close of that queue item is reversed -- closing is the human's call, this skill only proposes it, per .claude/skills/kiro-queue/SKILL.md:157. Amendment 2 (2026-07-27, corrected post-review same day): Requirement 14.2 revised so a developer field's own declared scale/offset is applied (decoding, not interpretation) -- see the amendments array for the ruling, the render-layer cross-spec consequence, and the post-review revision that fixed a critical render-layer regression the first commit introduced. The existing requirements.approved=true flag is left as-is (not re-flipped) but now covers wording ratified by the maintainer on 2026-07-27 for this one revised criterion; it does NOT constitute a fresh full-requirements review, and design.md/tasks.md approval remain unmet exactly as Amendment 1 left them -- this correction does not move any approval flag. TASKS REGENERATED IN MERGE MODE (2026-07-28, /kiro-spec-tasks fit-ingest -y). tasks.md now carries Amendment 1: majors 8-13 appended, 18 new executable units, first-pass majors 1-7 preserved BYTE-IDENTICALLY (the diff is 173 insertions and 0 deletions) along with every Implementation Note. A blockquote before task 8 states that 1-7 are the completed first pass, so the 24 [x] boxes are never again mistaken for amendment progress. All 98 criteria are mapped; Amendment 2 (Req 14.2) needed no task because it is already implemented inside unit 3.6. Two things a reader should not have to rediscover. (1) THE -y FLAG FLIPPED approvals.design FROM false TO true WITHOUT A HUMAN REVIEW IN THAT SESSION. That is a fast-track, not a ratification: the design's own gate history is /kiro-validate-design returning NO-GO on 2026-07-27, three findings fixed by an in-place revision, and that revision recording explicitly that it 'is not self-approval'. The two decisions design_revision_open_decisions flags for the maintainer -- the TrimpWeighting member NAMES (reported in every document via Req 17.6) and the two VerificationStatus vocabulary gaps owned by .kiro/queue/2026-07-27-banister-morton-primary-texts-obtained.md -- are NOT settled by this flag and remain open. (2) THE SOURCING TASK HAS A MACHINE-LOCAL PREREQUISITE the design did not state: neither primary text is committed. The Banister page scans (bannister_physiological_testing_of_the_high_performance_athlete/) and the Morton publisher PDF are .gitignore'd at the root of the primary checkout and are not redistributable, so a fresh worktree has NEITHER -- exactly like .fitdocs/data-root. docs/reference/banister-trimp-primary-sources.md IS committed and carries the extraction with page and equation numbers, but Req 15.5 forbids naming it as any constant's source, so it is evidence and not a citation target. Task 9.1 and a new Implementation Note both say so. INDEPENDENT TASK-GRAPH REVIEW, RUN LATE AND WORTH IT (2026-07-28, same day, after tasks.md had already merged). The kiro-spec-tasks Step 3.5 reviewer was SKIPPED on the original run -- the session read a session-prompt line as a standing user instruction not to dispatch subagents, took the skill's in-context fallback, and reported the omission as honoring a preference. It was not one; the line came from a server-delivered experiment payload, not from this repo (see the new Development Rules bullet in CLAUDE.md, 9df1d7b). A fresh reviewer subagent was then dispatched and returned NEEDS_FIXES with ten findings, every checkable one verified independently before being acted on. It found what an in-context review structurally could not: the parent had reasoned about design.md and never opened the test suite. Two were severe. (1) TASK 11 left the suite red in three places -- roughly sixteen direct calls to stress.trimp across tests/metrics/test_stress.py and test_facade.py, all comparing against a float while the return type becomes TrimpResult|None, plus test_facade.py's assertion that every derived field outside a named threshold list is identical with and without athlete inputs. The trap: the cheapest way to green that assertion is to report the default weighting UNCONDITIONALLY, which passes while destroying the very Req 17.6 invariant the task exists to establish. tasks.md now names the trap and the correct fix. (2) TASK 13.1 routed all value migration through snapshots, which is VACUOUS -- every committed snapshot reports no normalized power at all (the fixtures span ~9 s), while the real migration surface is the exact-value unit assertion pinned at 261.09384206589294. Both algorithms were recomputed over that test's own series: partial windows give exactly the pinned value, complete windows give 244.03877169307256, so the task as written sent an implementer into a hard failure with no instruction covering it. The task now states that the snapshots are vacuous here, that an unchanged snapshot is NOT evidence nothing moved, and that the mutation-discrimination comment and the two prose sites documenting the removed behavior move with it. Also repaired: 9.1's escape hatch contradicted Req 15.1/15.4/15.5 by permitting PRIMARY_TEXT records verified against the committed extraction (it now BLOCKS and escalates -- whether a prior reading discharges 15.1 is the maintainer's ruling, not the implementer's); 13.2 hid two cross-spec source edits and two foreign version tripwires, one of them a deliberate load/document drift pairing whose failure message asks for a ruling that task has no authority to make; 8.3's observable was numerically wrong (each golden carries TWO metric blocks, so two keys are added per file, not one) and omitted two field-contract pins; 13.4 shared 9.1's machine-local prerequisite and stated no alternative; 8.1's type-level observable sat outside the configured mypy perimeter; and 8.3 silently settled the still-open TrimpWeighting member-naming decision, now marked provisional in the task. Left as-is with a note rather than fixed: 12.1's completeness assertion is weaker than design.md's 'exactly once', because of the per-curve seam already open at 2026-07-28-weighting-terms-appear-twice-in-registry. Newly queued: 2026-07-28-root-public-surface-doc-unguarded. Requirement coverage re-verified mechanically after the repairs -- still 98/98, no phantom IDs, and no task added or removed. amendments.reason: Every numeric constant in the metrics package is cited to docs/reference/fitdocs-ai-reference.md §2, a working extraction from a secondary web source rather than a published methodology. src/fitdocs/load/channels/sources.py already records the consequence in its own module docstring: this module's TRIMP coefficients were 'cited only to docs/reference/fitdocs-ai-reference.md -- a secondary web source presented without qualification -- and that exact coefficient string was refuted 0-3 in adversarial verification'. That module marks BANISTER_TRIMP as SECONDARY_ATTESTATION and states that re-sourcing is out of its own feature's scope; this amendment is that re-sourcing, in the spec that owns the constants. Measured surface before deciding: _TRIMP_COEFFICIENT and _TRIMP_EXPONENT (stress.py:55,58), _TSS_SCALE (stress.py:61), _NP_MIN_SPAN_S and _NP_ROLLING_WINDOW_S (power.py:55,58), the NP averaging exponent (power.py, inline **4 / **0.25, not a named constant), _ALTITUDE_SMOOTHING_WINDOW (aggregates.py:238), and the moving-time threshold, which is not a named constant at all but the bare literal 0.5 at aggregates.py:103.
amendments.also: Three scope decisions ratified by the user before drafting. (1) SCOPE: every fit-ingest constant citing §2, not TRIMP alone -- stress.py, power.py and aggregates.py. The §3 chart figures in render/charts/ are presentation choices owned by workout-docs and stay out. (2) SEX-SPECIFIC WEIGHTING: Banister's weighting is sex-specific in the primary literature while fit-ingest applies one pair to every athlete and calls it 'sex-neutral' in its own docstring; the weighting becomes a caller-supplied selection (Req 17) defaulting to the current pair when absent, so no athlete's number changes unless they state a selection. (3) UNOBTAINABLE PRIMARY TEXT BLOCKS: Req 15.4 does NOT permit the honest-downgrade-to-SECONDARY_ATTESTATION pattern that MINETTI_2002 and BANISTER_TRIMP set one layer down. Banister (1991) is a book chapter and Morton (1990) is a paywalled journal paper, so an unsatisfiable requirement is a live risk; it was raised before drafting and the choice was reaffirmed. Migration is by regeneration (Req 18), which is the story sync.py:96 already establishes: 'regeneration is the upgrade, there is no in-place transform.'
amendments.revision: 2026-07-26, at the design gate, before any design was drafted. Amendment 1 as first committed (22cc143) was unsatisfiable by construction: Req 15.6 enumerates seven items -- the training-impulse weighting counts as one item though it names two constants, the coefficient and the exponent, so the enumeration covers eight named constants in all -- and Req 15.1 required each to be read from 'the published work that defines them', but three of the seven items are defined by no published work at all -- the moving-time movement threshold (the bare literal 0.5 at aggregates.py:103), _NP_MIN_SPAN_S (power.py:55, fitdocs' own choice of when to refuse to report normalized power), and _ALTITUDE_SMOOTHING_WINDOW (aggregates.py:238, whose only cited source is the very docs/reference/ document Req 15.5 forbids naming). Req 15.7 exempts only values carrying no methodological choice, which a movement threshold carries, so Req 15.4 blocked the feature on a primary text that could never be obtained because none was ever written. The user ratified adding a fitdocs-chosen category rather than narrowing 15.6 or accepting the block. Criteria 15.8, 15.9 and 16.7 added; 15.1, 15.4, 15.6 and 16.4 scoped to match. NO criterion renumbered or withdrawn, and Req 15.4's bar over Banister, Morton and Coggan is untouched -- recording a secondary attestation remains forbidden. The category reuses the semantics of VerificationStatus.FITDOCS_MEASURED at src/fitdocs/load/channels/sources.py:60 rather than inventing a fourth vocabulary. Req 15.9 requires the conclusion that no published work defines a value to itself be recorded with what was searched, so the new category cannot become a cheaper answer than obtaining a text that exists. Requirement count is unchanged at 18; criterion count rises from 95 to 98.
amendments.cross_spec: Req 17.3 keeps the weighting selection a caller-supplied argument and explicitly forbids fit-ingest reading it from athlete profile data or configuration -- athlete profile storage is out of this spec's scope. Whichever spec owns src/fitdocs/athlete.py (athlete-benchmarks is actively extending it) decides whether to store and prompt for the field; fit-ingest works unchanged if it never does, since Req 17.2 defaults to the pre-amendment pair. Req 18.1-18.3 place obligations on the document layer, not on this library: the document-format version advance, the regen rewrite and the audit staleness report are all owned by wiki-contract/workout-docs, and Req 18.5 restates that fit-ingest still writes nothing. A DOC_VERSION bump is required only if the re-sourced values actually differ (Req 18.4).
amendments.design: 2026-07-26, generated at the design gate after requirements auto-approval. Three decisions a reviewer should check first, recorded in full in research.md as D1-D5. (1) VOCABULARY OWNERSHIP -- the queue item 2026-07-26-citation-vocabulary-diverges-across-layers explicitly handed this design phase the question of who owns VerificationStatus/Citation once fit-ingest also needs them, since fit-ingest is UPSTREAM of load-channels and cannot import fitdocs.load.channels.sources. Answer: they move to a dependency-free src/fitdocs/citation.py and load.channels.sources re-exports them, so exactly one vocabulary exists. That edit is import-only -- no record, status, note, Divergence or Req 8 obligation of load-channels changes, and tests/load/channels/test_sources.py passing UNMODIFIED is the design's evidence. Whether load-channels adopts Req 15.4's ban on SECONDARY_ATTESTATION is deliberately NOT decided here and stays with that queue item. (2) DOC_VERSION -- Req 18.2 and 18.3 need no new code (audit.py:213 already reports a below-version document stale and sync.py:1183 already rewrites it from source), so the only new act is the conditional bump in contract.py, which lands in this spec's implementation because Req 18.1 makes it a completion condition. CitedConstant.previous_value is the machine-readable answer to Req 18.4 and the guard asserts the coupling in both directions. (3) NO DESIGN-PHASE SOURCING -- the constants' values were deliberately not web-searched, because establishing a value from search results is the secondary-summary path Req 15.4 forbids; feasibility is expressed as a gate with a defined block and sourcing is the first implementation task, so a block surfaces before dependent work exists. Banister (1991) and Morton (1990) remain the named, accepted schedule risk. One discrepancy surfaced and was queued rather than silently resolved: criterion 15.6 enumerates EIGHT constants across SEVEN items -- the training-impulse weighting is one item naming two constants, the coefficient and the exponent -- while the amendment narrative called them seven without stating that reading (proposed resolution, awaiting maintainer confirmation: .kiro/queue/2026-07-26-amendment-1-constant-count-ambiguous.md, requirements.md's narrative now states it explicitly). The design classifies all eight; the enumeration governs.
amendments.design_revision: 2026-07-27, at the design gate, after /kiro-validate-design fit-ingest returned NO-GO. The design was NOT regenerated; it was revised in place for three findings plus one maintainer ruling. NOTHING in requirements.md changed and approvals.requirements stays approved. (1) Req 15.2 WAS UNREPRESENTABLE. CitedConstant.source was single-valued with the stated invariant that a constant with two sources cannot be constructed, so 15.2's 'Banister (1991) AND Morton (1990) ... together with the locator within each work' had no mechanism and no guard -- it appeared only as a traceability row naming two records that nothing bound to a constant. Latent when drafted; concrete once the texts were read and found to disagree. FIX: one governing source plus corroborators -- new Corroboration and Agreement types in citation.py, CitedConstant.corroborators, and the guard assertions 15.2 never had. 16.2's 'exactly one record' survives because the governing source stays single; research.md D6 records the alternatives, including the maintainer's stated willingness to accept PRIMARY_TEXT plus a prose note. (2) THE SOURCING GATE WAS STALE. The design still presented Banister/Morton as an unobtained, accepted schedule risk and expected a record named ALLEN_COGGAN. Both are superseded on main: the maintainer supplied both texts 2026-07-27 and both were read in full (docs/reference/banister-trimp-primary-sources.md), and the work actually obtained for the three power constants is COGGAN 2003 -- Coggan's own USA Cycling chapter, already shipping as COGGAN_TSS with PRIMARY_TEXT at load/channels/sources.py:137 -- not the Allen & Coggan book, whose text was never obtained. FIX: the classification table is now RESOLVED rather than expected, with governing source, locator and corroborator per constant; ALLEN_COGGAN -> COGGAN_2003; the accepted-risk section records what is now sourced and by whom; D4 is superseded in place rather than deleted, because its reasoning (never establish a value from search results) still holds and nothing here rests on a search. Two traps are now named in the design: B91's three printed worked examples all contradict its own equation, and B91 misstates e as 2.712. (3) REQ 17 IS ABOUT SEX AND THE DESIGN NEVER SAID SO -- zero occurrences of 'sex' in an 84 KB document whose Req 17 objective opens 'As an athlete whose sex the training-impulse model distinguishes'. With the text read, the member set and default are no longer deferrable: B91 p. 408 defines male (0.64, 1.92) and female (0.86, 1.67), and Req 17.2 pins the default to the pre-amendment pair, so DEFAULT_TRIMP_WEIGHTING IS the male curve and Req 17.6 makes DerivedMetrics.trimp_weighting report it for every athlete who states nothing -- which Req 17.3 guarantees is everyone, since nothing may store the selection between runs. FIX: members fixed as BANISTER_MALE / BANISTER_FEMALE (the prefix is deliberate -- a member names which fitted curve, not the athlete), the default stated as a consequence of 17.2, a DEPARTURES entry for the sex-neutral application (16.5), and an Out of Boundary paragraph handing workout-docs the presentation decision WITH the consequence stated. THE MEMBER NAMING IS FLAGGED FOR THE MAINTAINER, not settled by the design. (4) MAINTAINER RULING, NP WINDOW START: adopt Coggan's step 1 fully -- the rolling mean emits only complete windows, dropping the partial-window averages over the first 29 points that power.py:87-101 emits today. That behaviour was never sourced from any text, so it is removed rather than recorded as a Departure fitdocs has no reason to defend (research.md D7). THIS IS THE ONLY VALUE-MOVING CHANGE IN AMENDMENT 1 and it reverses the 'no migration owed' reading that followed from the 0.64 ruling: NP rises, carrying IF, VI, TSS and bike EF, so DOC_VERSION 3 -> 4 is now UNCONDITIONAL, every committed document goes stale until regenerated, and the regeneration rehearsal runs unconditionally instead of in a branch that would never be taken. It also forced a MigrationGate correction: coupling the bump to previous_value alone was WRONG, since here a value moves with every previous_value still None -- the gate now asserts two independent triggers and concludes 'no bump' only when both are quiet. Req 8.4 mandates 'a trailing rolling mean' and is silent on the start condition, so this refines an underspecified criterion rather than contradicting one and no requirements amendment is strictly owed; that the behaviour has no criterion of its own is queued at 2026-07-28-np-window-start-has-no-criterion.md, which notes closing it reopens requirements approval.
amendments.design_revision_open_decisions: Two things the design flags rather than settles, both for the maintainer. (1) TrimpWeighting member NAMES -- BANISTER_MALE / BANISTER_FEMALE is the design's choice and its reasoning is stated, but the field is reported in every document via Req 17.6 and the name is what an athlete sees. (2) The VerificationStatus vocabulary gaps this work surfaced -- 'primary text, but a companion primary text disagrees' and the split attestation where B91's chapter is primary text while its 1991 year rests on the OCLC/Internet Archive catalogue record (the book's copyright page carries no year). Corroboration answers the first for CITATION purposes but adds no VerificationStatus term; the second is a per-field question Corroboration does not touch. Both stay owned by .kiro/queue/2026-07-27-banister-morton-primary-texts-obtained.md; Citation.year stays a plain int and citation.py is the only module a later ruling would edit.

amendments.reason: Queue item 2026-07-25-devfield-declared-scale-ignored: a FIT field_description message can declare a scale and/or offset for a developer field, but garmin-fit-sdk parses both into its field profile and never applies them to a developer field -- only to a native profile field (decoder.py's __apply_scale_and_offset, called only from __apply_profile). extract_developer_fields therefore returned a raw, wrong-by-a-constant-factor value whenever a writer declared either. Latent, not active: all six developer-field descriptors across the 74-file corpus declare scale=None. Req 14.2 as worded ('pass developer-field values through as decoded ... without interpretation, derivation, or renaming') was broad enough to endorse the gap rather than close it.
amendments.also: The maintainer's ruling (2026-07-27), applied directly rather than re-litigated: applying a scale/offset the file ITSELF declares is decoding -- the identical act garmin-fit-sdk already performs for a native profile field, using the FIT-protocol formula value / scale - offset (confirmed by reading decoder.py:__apply_scale_and_offset, not assumed). Inferring an UNDECLARED convention (the AVG METs hundredths defect this same investigation surfaced) remains interpretation and stays forbidden; Req 14.2 is revised to draw that line explicitly rather than leave it ambiguous. Requirements 14.1, 14.3, 14.4 are unaffected. No criterion renumbered.
amendments.implementation: Implemented directly in the same change (src/fitdocs/ingest/summary.py: extract_developer_fields, _developer_value, _scale_one) with synthetic field_description fixtures (no corpus file declares a scale) -- the current corpus's shape (both scale and offset undeclared) is preserved byte-identically via the same undeclared-defaults-to-identity arithmetic, not a separate code path. Edge cases handled explicitly and each pinned by a sole-failure mutation: scale=0 (SUPERSEDED -- see the revision key below: this originally fell back to the raw value; the maintainer ruled on 2026-07-27 that the field is OMITTED instead, since a raw value presented as scaled is the wrong-by-a-constant-factor shape CLAUDE.md forbids); offset declared without scale (applies against an implicit scale of 1); a declared scale on an array value (applied element-wise, matching the SDK's own per-element treatment of a native array field); a non-numeric raw value under a declared scale, e.g. a string-typed developer field (passes through un-scaled rather than raising). design.md's SummaryExtractor entry and traceability row for 14.1-14.4 updated to match; this is a source-only correction of an implemented, unshipped-behavior-change unit -- no execution-unit count or design-gate approval affected.
amendments.cross_spec: Alters the contract of Activity.developer_fields: a value MAY now differ from the raw wire integer when its own field_description declares a scale/offset (Req 14.2, as amended), and a described scale=0 field (post-review ruling below) is OMITTED from the mapping entirely rather than present with a raw value -- a shape change, not only a value change. Both training-load and workout-docs are Activity.developer_fields consumers named in this spec's Boundary Context; training-load reads none of the current corpus's six described fields today, but workout-docs' render/sections.py (Req 6.7 supplemental rows) does, for exactly the two keys the AVG METs defect investigation was about (SESSION WEATHER HUMIDITY, AVG METs). The post-review revision below adds Activity.developer_fields_declared_scale (a frozenset[str] of keys ingest decoded via a declared scale/offset) precisely so render/sections.py can consume this contract change safely -- see that revision's own note and workout-docs/design.md's Supplemental values entry, both updated in the same branch. A second, accepted downstream consequence: contract.py's format_session_uuid requires SESSION UUID as a 16-int tuple, and a declared scale on that field would coerce its elements to float, making format_session_uuid return None and the frontmatter uuid key omitted -- this fails CLOSED (no fabrication) so it is acceptable, but is recorded here as a second cross-spec effect rather than silently discovered later.
amendments.revision: 2026-07-27, post-review (same day). Review of the first commit (1b52bc8 (rebased from the pre-review SHA f73fa99)) found: (1) CRITICAL -- render/sections.py's _SUPPLEMENTALS fallback applied its own hundredths-guess factor unconditionally, so a writer that actually declares a scale would have its already-correct, ingest-decoded value silently multiplied by 0.01 a second time on the rendered page (measured: 9.5 in Activity.developer_fields rendered as 0.1); no test exercised a declared scale through the render layer, which is what let this ship. FIXED by Activity.developer_fields_declared_scale (a frozenset[str] the maintainer ruled should surface DECLAREDNESS ONLY, not the full field description -- units/components/bits/accumulate stay queued) and render/sections.py consulting it before applying its fallback; pinned by tests/render/test_sections.py::test_declared_scale_developer_field_is_not_double_scaled through parse_fit end-to-end. (2) Criterion 14.2 as first revised prescribed division by zero for a DECLARED scale=0 ('defaulting an undeclared term to its identity' does not cover a declared one) and left the non-numeric passthrough undocumented outside a docstring; the maintainer RULED scale=0 OMITS the field entirely (not the raw-value fallback the first commit shipped) -- the raw fallback would have reinstated the wrong-by-a-constant-factor, no-signal shape the originating queue item condemned, against CLAUDE.md's absent-data-is-None rule and this requirement's own Criterion 14.4. Both are now stated in Criterion 14.2 itself, not only in summary.py's docstrings, and each is pinned by its own test. (3) The 'byte-identical' claim in summary.py and the original commit message was overstated for bool: _developer_value(True, None, None) returned the int 1 on the first commit (bool is an int subclass), defeating sections.py's own isinstance(value, bool) guard; _scale_one now returns an unchanged value (preserving type) whenever nothing is actually applied, restoring true byte/type identity for every type the pre-existing pass-through handled, pinned by test_undeclared_bool_value_preserves_its_type. No criterion is renumbered; Requirement count and criterion count are unchanged.
